brief:
Record Palestinian turnout in Israel's recent elections has created an opening to remove Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from power, Mondoweiss reported. However, analysts caution that a change in Israeli leadership may not substantially alter the occupation or shift Israel's core policies toward Palestinians.

The question now facing Palestinians is whether a new Israeli government, should one emerge from the opposition's gains, would meaningfully improve their circumstances or merely represent a shift in personnel without substantive policy change.
dek: Record Palestinian turnout in Israel's elections may soon end Netanyahu’s rule, but the "opposition" will not end the occupation or fundamentally change Israel’s policies. So, what will a new Israeli government actually mean for Palestinians?
title: Palestinian voters in Israel turn election against Netanyahu, uncertain what comes next
